findings.title: A delivered book as public disclosure
findings.claim: The book and its descent are framed as a communicative transfer that draws people toward visible guidance: the following verses describe messengers making a message plain, repeat the extraction formula for Moses' people, and name denial and path-blocking as resistance to that movement.
findings.mechanism: The focus book carries written-text and delivered-message meanings, while the focus extraction and light supply the movement and destination. The messenger-language and clarification in 14:4 make the delivered text publicly intelligible; 14:5 reenacts the same movement for a named community. The disbeliever and obstruction contexts in 14:2-3 set denial and resistance against disclosure, so the scene changes from a book as information alone to a message that moves people into a perceptible and followable direction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the Book is described through an act of bringing people out and into light, and why opposition is pictured as concealment or obstruction while the ordinary guidance reading remains intact.
findings.containment: The pericope supports spatial and communal disclosure as an added image. It does not make every darkness literal concealment, every book a physical writing event, or every disbeliever an agent of concealment.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel supports are corroborated by exact pericope text, but the concealment and cross-root contacts remain contextual readings rather than lexical equations.

findings.title: A traversed route under obstruction
findings.claim: The pericope turns the focus route into a practical course whose access can be blocked, bent, and lost from, while later guidance restores orientation. The road and light meet the context's extended path, diversion, sought crookedness, and distant misguidance; 14:12 returns to people relying on God after being guided along their ways.
findings.mechanism: The focus road provides a traversable carrier and the focus light supplies visibility. The 14:3 context supplies a distinct path that people obstruct and deliberately seek to bend, while 14:12 names guidance along ways and persistence under harm. Their contact changes the path from a destination label into a route that travelers must be able to follow and that opponents can interfere with. The bending can remain physical or abstract without choosing between them.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that route, beacon, blockage, curvature, and loss of bearing are different operations: the focus offers orientation, while the surrounding verses show that orientation can be contested and resumed.
findings.containment: The path remains the path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy. The evidence does not establish water access or easy terrain, and the physical and metaphorical bend remain live contextual possibilities without a verdict.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence aligns with the supplied Arabic in 14:3 and 14:12; the physical-versus-abstract bend is kept as contextual possibility and unsupported water/ground facets are excluded.

Its context roles then distinguish active diversion, the extended path being obstructed, intentional seeking, altered geometry, and the downstream loss of direction. Their sequence changes the before-reading of darkness as passive lack of guidance into an after-reading where darkness may be maintained by redirecting travelers and deforming the route.

findings.containment: The packet itself names the live alternative: 14:3 may describe opposition to the path without defining the focus darknesses. The route-sabotage reading is therefore attributed and contextual, not an exhaustive definition of every darkness.

epistemic.reason: The HFT anchor coverage is complete and the exact Arabic supports the surface contacts, but reader identity and context roots/indices are legacy-unbound and remain attributed.

findings.title: A communal exit sustained by memory
findings.claim: The focus movement from darkness to light can also name collective emancipation: 14:5 repeats it for Moses' people, 14:6 describes oppression and rescue, and 14:5-7 join remembrance, divine commitment, gratitude, and increase to keep that exit operative. The focus darknesses also carry the related images of withheld rights and wrongful treatment.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace says the focus darknesses can be anchored in withholding, then tracks the repeated causative exit, remembrance, rescue, imposed evil, and slaughter in the Moses sequence. The people who are extracted become a named community; their remembered days connect the rescue to the past, while the focus permission meets a later announced commitment and gratitude is followed by increase. Together these contacts change the before-reading of darkness and light as chiefly belief and knowledge into a live social-political reading of organized domination and collective emancipation, without removing guidance.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the darkness-to-light formula enacted in a community's release from oppression, with memory and gratitude giving the achieved exit continuity rather than leaving it as a single past event.
findings.containment: The Moses sequence is one concrete enactment, not an exhaustive definition of every darkness or every guidance event. The exact context text grounds the historical analogy; the HFT reader identity and unresolved branch mappings remain attributed, and gratitude is not equated with liberation.

epistemic.reason: All HFT anchors are present and exact Arabic verifies their surface contact, but the reader identity and several branch records are legacy-unbound or unresolved, so their contextual roles remain attributed.

findings.title: Permission under ownership and care
findings.claim: The focus permission comes from a Lord whose ownership is immediately described as comprehensive; the Moses sequence also shows rescue as a blessing from the Lord and follows gratitude with increase. Together these contacts let the permission be read within both sovereign authority and continuing care.
findings.mechanism: The focus word rabbihim carries ownership and governing authority as well as nurturing meanings. The next ayah says that all in the heavens and earth belong to God, contacting the ownership facet; the supplied 14:6-7 context then moves from rescue and blessing to promised increase after gratitude, contacting the nurturing facets. This changes permission from a single isolated grant into a direction from the owner-ruler who also raises and sustains the community.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the plain authorization sense while perceiving the Lord's permission as both sovereign and sustaining across the pericope.
findings.containment: The context adds ownership and nurture to the focus relation; it does not reduce permission to coercion, make the focus noun mean a contract, or claim every permission is a growth process.

epistemic.reason: The ownership context is exact, while the rescue and increase roles are supplied through complete but legacy-unbound HFT evidence.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Sahiplik, buyruk yetkisi ve yönetip düzenleme aynı çekirdekte birleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus construct rabbihim names their Lord and can carry ownership, command authority, and governance.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 14:2 says everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's permission meets the adjacent ownership statement, making the authorization a direction from the comprehensive owner and governor.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The route proceeds by the permission of the one whose ownership encompasses all.
branch_activations.boundary: The contextual relation does not reduce the focus title to property ownership alone.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Süreç, gözetilen şeyi eksik durumdan tamamlanmış duruma doğru geliştirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus Lord can carry the branch's sense of developing what is under care toward completion.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied context links rescue from Pharaoh's people with a blessing and then with promised increase after gratitude.
branch_activations.activation: Rescue and later increase contact the focus Lord as a continuing source of care, not only a one-time permission.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The Lord's relation to the people can be read as raising them out of an incomplete and oppressed state toward flourishing.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a contextual reading of the Lord title; the verse still says permission, not education or growth as its literal verb.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Büyüyen varlık beslenir ve gelişmesi sağlanır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus Lord can be the one who nourishes and enables growth.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 14:7 context promises increase after gratitude.
branch_activations.activation: The promised increase contacts the Lord title as nourishment and growth, coloring the focus's permission with continuing provision.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The route's authorization can also be seen within a relation that develops and increases its recipients.
branch_activations.boundary: This branch adds an image of growth; it does not make the focus word a verb of increase or identify the increase with a material substance.

findings.title: The destination under rejection and tyranny
findings.claim: The focus path ends with the Mighty and the Praiseworthy; the pericope later calls God praiseworthy even if everyone disbelieves and ends with every obstinate tyrant failing. Those returns make the destination's praise independent of human response and let its might meet resistance.
findings.mechanism: The focus epithets provide the carriers. The immediate context repeats al-Hamid beside God's self-sufficiency under possible universal disbelief, while the pericope's closing line says every tyrant obstinate fails. The explicit epithet echo and the later failure of tyrants contact the focus destination, changing its descriptions from concluding titles into qualities shown to persist through rejection and opposition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the named destination as praiseworthy even without human approval and as a source of might against obstinate resistance.
findings.containment: The Hamid echo is explicit in the supplied Arabic. The later tyrant's failure does not explicitly name al-Aziz as its grammatical agent, so the relation to the focus might remains a pericope-level resonance.

epistemic.reason: The target Arabic and both connection records are supplied, but the focus-to-tyrant relation is inferential and the 14:15 connection is labeled weak for marginal contribution.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: yermenin karşıtı olan, iyilik için teşekkürü de kapsayan övgü
branch_activations.facet_statement: İyi sözlerle övme, yermenin karşıtıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus epithet al-Hamid describes one who is praiseworthy.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 14:8 repeats the same epithet while saying God is free of need even if everyone disbelieves.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated epithet meets the statement of self-sufficiency under disbelief, making praise independent of whether people respond.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The destination's praiseworthiness remains even when human belief or gratitude is absent.
branch_activations.boundary: The contextual echo reinforces the focus epithet; it does not make the path or its travelers the object of praise.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Güç, korunmuşluk ve saygınlık kişiyi yenilmekten ve aşağılanmaktan uzak tutar.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus epithet al-Aziz carries enduring strength and inviolability.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The pericope closes by saying that every obstinate tyrant fails.
branch_activations.activation: The focus might meets the failure of tyrants, letting the destination's strength be heard against persistent opposition.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The path leads toward an authority whose might is not overcome by tyrannical resistance.
branch_activations.boundary: The context does not make al-Aziz the explicit grammatical subject of the tyrant's failure.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir taraf karşısındakini yenerek onun üzerinde üstünlük kurar.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus epithet al-Aziz can also carry the branch's relational image of one side overcoming another.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied closing context says every obstinate tyrant fails.
branch_activations.activation: The failure of an opposing tyrant meets the branch's overcoming relation and returns it to the focus epithet.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The destination's might can be read as superiority over resistance, in addition to enduring strength.
branch_activations.boundary: This relational sense is contextual and does not assign the focus epithet as the explicit actor in 14:15.
